item.title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
item.description:
Authors: Frank T Wen, Kyler Rosen, Siddhi Ramesh, Michael Koo, Sara Kochanny, Sasha Jain-Liu, Emma Dyer, Alexander T Pearson

Pathology foundation models underpin a growing number of histology-based cancer biomarkers, but sensitivity to slide scanner-specific image signatures degrades cross-center reliability and reproducibility. We developed a foundation model fine-tuning method that improved consistency in head-and-neck cancer human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction, colorectal cancer microsatellite instability (MSI) identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. This tempering method decreased cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% for HPV (95% CI 59.0-73.9%), 69.3% for MSI (95% CI 51.

item.title: Evaluation of Machine-Learning Weather Models in Reproducing Mesoscale Tornado-Favorable Convective Environments
item.description:
Authors: Yiding Luo, Rui Yuan, Shetian Xia, Royce Lee, Alexandra Anderson-Frey

Machine-learning (ML)-based weather prediction models have developed rapidly in recent years and are already being used in operational weather forecasting. These ML-based models' performance has exceeded that of traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP) methods in certain implementations, with substantially lower computational cost. However, most ML-based models were trained on global data at a horizontal grid spacing of 0.25 degrees, which may be too coarse to capture tornado-favorable parameters

item.title: Latent Channel Completion for Forecasting in Sensor Networks with Failed Detectors
item.description:
Authors: Mehran Shabanpour, Sadaf Khademi, Maryam Hosseini, Haiyan Xu, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis, Arash Mohammadi

Monitoring networks for traffic and utility infrastructure lose sensors routinely, and forecasting models that couple sensors together to gain accuracy also inherit an exposure to those losses. When a detector stops reporting, the substituted value is embedded as though it were a reading and propagates through the shared representation that couples the network, degrading forecasts for sensors that are still healthy. Because these models are selected on benchmarks where every sensor reports, the exposure is absent from the numbers used to choose them

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。
- 任务：降尺度/预报/临近预测等应用场景。

item.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
item.description:
Authors: Arya Sikder, Sriram Pillutla

A foundation model for time series is pretrained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. Such datasets are scarce, and a few public leaderboards carry most comparisons, yet none of them states how small a difference its datasets can detect. We call that quantity the resolution of a board and introduce Vernier, a tool that computes it from the files a board already publishes

item.title: Bayesian Data Integration and Model Updating in Probabilistic Digital Twins
item.description:
Authors: Dafydd Cotoarbă, Antonis Mavritsakis, Timo Schweckendiek, Ian FC Smith, Daniel Straub

This paper proposes a framework for sequential Bayesian updating in probabilistic digital twins using data from multiple sources collected over time. The framework distinguishes between property data and behavior data, according to how observations relate to the digital state. Property data directly inform a subset of the uncertain model parameters and can therefore be incorporated using efficient dedicated Bayesian updating methods

item.title: Boundary Representation-Driven Graph Transformer Modeling for Machining Operation Sequencing
item.description:
Authors: Fatemeh Elhambakhsh, Gaurav Ameta, Aditi Roy, Hyunwoong Ko

Machining process planning is inherently complex due to the interdependence between part geometry, machining operations, and evolving manufacturable states. Traditional approaches rely heavily on expert knowledge and rule-based systems, limiting scalability and automation. While recent machine learning methods have shown promise, most operate on simplified geometric representations, such as voxels or hand-crafted features, which fail to fully exploit the rich geometric and topological information encoded in Boundary Representation (B-Rep) models

item.title: Tokenization and Architecture Jointly Allocate Component Roles in Time Series Transformers
item.description:
Authors: Mingyu Kim, Doguk Kim

Time series transformers have achieved strong forecasting performance, yet it remains unclear which of their components, attention or the feed-forward network (FFN), constructs temporal features, and how tokenization such as patching changes this. We propose a temporal probing framework that uses 15 token-level diagnostic tasks to measure feature construction as the gain in linear decodability of temporal properties from one sub-layer to the next (a matched MLP probe already saturates at the embedding). It targets models whose probed representations are read by a linear forecasting head

item.title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning
item.description:
Authors: Shadieh Mohammadi, Koorosh Aslansefat

Conventional post-hoc explanation methods were developed largely for non-spatial inputs and often provide limited explicit treatment of geographic context. We introduce Geo-SMILE, a model-agnostic framework that distinguishes substantive Feature explanation from geographic-position response through complementary perturbation branches. The Feature branch masks substantive predictors while retaining observed coordinates; the Geo branch relocates geographic units while holding substantive predictors fixed

item.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
item.description:
Authors: Han-Yi Lin, Kieran Griperay, Qiang Zhou, Xiangyu Zhou, Nate Bonacci, Zinachidi Achikeh, Li He, Shaofei Qi

Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。

item.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
item.description:
Authors: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Jaehoon Lee, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim

Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy. However, existing works have two limitations: 1) TSFMs reduce the predictive distribution to its median or mean, flattening diverse futures into a calm line, and 2) multimodal TS forecasting models incorporate text into the forecaster through TS-language alignment, which is substantially weaker than vision-language alignment. item.title: Gaze World Model
item.description:
Authors: Jiawen Zhang, Houze Yang, Xu Cao, Yifan Shen, Zhongyi Zhou, Steve Wong, Ismini Lourentzou, Inki Kim

Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode

item.description:
Authors: Hanbin Ko, Hong-Jun Choi, Jihun Kim, Young-Gon Kim, Dongheon Lee, Chang Min Park

Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it

item.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study
item.description:
Authors: Haimanot Bitew, Ayisheshim Almaw, Habtamu Zegeye, Demeke Alene

Species-level differentiation of Plasmodium falciparum (PF) and P. vivax (PV) determines treatment, yet deep learning detectors rarely test whether their explanations are reliable. In this pilot feasibility study of TRACE-Mal, a research prototype combining YOLOv8n-seg detection and a six-model soft-voting ensemble, we examined whether agreement among three post-hoc explanation methods (Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP) is associated with the correctness of species calls

item.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
item.description:
Authors: Zhifei Zhu, Hongtao Zhang, Yu Ren, Wei Zhou, Zeping Xie, Yi He

EEG analysis spans choosing alternatives, judging statements, and rating ordered attributes, requiring calibratable probabilities with explicit meaning. We present EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model for EEG. Given an EEG window, a question and an answer specification, one forward pass returns a typed readout: CHOICE gives a candidate distribution, NOUL a proposition probability, and SCORE an ordered-level distribution and expectation
